q: In the weight-of-rebar formula W = D² × L × ____, with D in mm and L in m, what is the constant?
n: 0.006165 is about 1/162, from the steel density of 7,850 kg/m³. W comes out in kilograms.
formula: W (kg) = D² × L × 0.006165   (D in mm, L in m)
ref: PNS 49 - unit mass of deformed steel bars; steel density 7,850 kg/m3

q: In the angle-bar weight formula W = (Leg₁ + Leg₂ − t) × t × L × ____, with legs and t in mm and L in m, what is the constant?
n: 0.00785 comes from the 7,850 kg/m³ density of steel. W comes out in kilograms.
formula: W (kg) = (Leg₁ + Leg₂ − t) × t × L × 0.00785   (mm, mm, mm, m)
ref: ASEP Steel Handbook - unit mass of angle bars; steel density 7,850 kg/m3

q: Estimating practice adds a compaction allowance to fill volume. What factor corresponds to a 10% allowance?
n: A 10% compaction allowance multiplies the required fill volume by 1.10. The allowance depends on the soil, so use the factor the problem states.
formula: Volume to order = Volume of earthfill × 1.10
ref: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate - earthwork, shrinkage and compaction allowance

q: A fill of 250 cu.m. is needed. Using a 10% compaction allowance, what volume of earthfill should be estimated?
ref: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate - earthwork, shrinkage and compaction allowance

q: A concrete vibrator needs about 2 minutes per sqm. What area can it cover in one hour?
n: 60 min ÷ 2 min per sqm = 30 sqm per hour.
formula: Area per hour = 60 min ÷ minutes per sqm
ref: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate - equipment output, concrete vibrator
